description: Tang Yuan Glutinous Rice Balls are a classic Chinese dessert, symbolizing togetherness and completeness. These soft, chewy rice balls, often filled with sweet black sesame paste, are traditionally enjoyed during festivals like the Lantern Festival and Winter Solstice. Served in a fragrant ginger syrup, they offer a comforting and delightful taste of Chinese culinary heritage.

instructions.title: Prepare the Black Sesame Filling
instructions.text: Toast black sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until fragrant. Let them cool slightly, then grind them into a fine powder using a food processor or mortar and pestle. In a bowl, combine the ground sesame seeds with granulated sugar and melted lard or butter. Mix well until a thick paste forms. Chill the filling in the refrigerator for 5 minutes to firm up, making it easier to handle.

instructions.title: Make the Glutinous Rice Dough
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, gradually add warm water to the glutinous rice flour while mixing with your hands or a spoon. Continue adding water until a soft, pliable dough forms. Knead the dough for about 3-5 minutes until it is smooth and no longer sticky. If the dough is too dry, add a little more water; if too wet, add a little more flour. Cover the dough with a damp cloth to prevent it from drying out.

instructions.title: Form the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Divide the chilled black sesame filling into small portions, about 1 teaspoon each, and roll them into small balls. Take a small piece of glutinous rice dough, about 15-20g, and flatten it into a disc in your palm. Place one sesame filling ball in the center of the dough disc. Gently bring the edges of the dough up and around the filling, pinching to seal completely. Roll the filled dough into a smooth, round ball. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ginger Syrup
instructions.text: In a medium saucepan, combine the sliced fresh ginger, brown sugar, and 500ml of water. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for at least 25 minutes. This allows the ginger flavor to fully infuse into the syrup. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired.

instructions.title: Cook the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully drop the formed tang yuan into the boiling water, stirring gently to prevent them from sticking to the bottom. Once the tang yuan float to the surface, continue to cook for another 2-3 minutes until they appear plump and translucent. This ensures they are cooked through.

instructions.title: Serve the Tang Yuan
instructions.text: Using a slotted spoon, carefully transfer the cooked tang yuan directly from the boiling water into the simmering ginger syrup. Serve the Tang Yuan hot in individual bowls, ensuring each serving gets a few rice balls and a generous amount of fragrant ginger syrup. Enjoy immediately as a comforting dessert.

tips: To achieve perfectly chewy tang yuan, use warm water when mixing the glutinous rice flour. This helps create a more pliable and smoother dough.
For a richer filling, replace lard with unsalted butter or coconut oil. You can also add a pinch of salt to balance the sweetness of the sesame filling.
Tang Yuan are best enjoyed immediately after cooking. If you have leftovers, store them in the ginger syrup in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stove.
